subject: English
passage: In the early days of the internet in the 1990s, many people expected that online shopping would quickly replace traditional retail stores, much like catalog shopping had supplemented in-person purchases. But major retailers were reluctant to establish significant online presences, especially during a period when concerns about credit card security on the internet were widespread. Companies like Sears and JCPenney needed to convince customers to trust online transactions despite not yet having reliable systems to guarantee secure payment processing.
prompt: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined phrase in the text as a whole?

choices.A: It identifies a specific reason behind some retailers' reluctance to embrace online commerce.
choices.B: It contrasts the development of online shopping with the development of catalog shopping.
choices.C: It describes how companies attempted to persuade customers to shop online.
choices.D: It explains why a particular type of online service was successful at the time.

explanation:
Choice A is the best answer because it accurately describes the function of the underlined phrase in the text as a whole. According to the text, retailers were reluctant to establish online presences in the early days of internet shopping. The underlined phrase then indicates that this reluctance was partly due to widespread concerns about credit card security on the internet. Thus, the underlined phrase identifies a specific reason behind some retailers' reluctance to embrace online commerce.

Why D is incorrect:

Choice D is incorrect. The underlined phrase focuses on a reason retailers were reluctant to embrace online commerce, not what types of online services were successful.
